Patch Notes[/h2][p][/p][h3][b]PvP Province - Lyonesse[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The PvP Province has been redone and is now much larger.[/p][/*][*][p]Added unique landmark locations, such as ruined old cities, to hint at the history of the province.[/p][/*][*][p]Added new sites in the form of watchtowers, providing a convenient place for players to repair their gear and craft items.[/p][/*][*][p]Fast Travel is now enabled within Lyonesse between the ruined cities and province gateways. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Crafting & resources[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added two new resources exclusive to the PvP province: Ambergrasp and Canonite.[/p][/*][*][p]Enchantment of gear: the new resources found in Lyonesse can be refined in the Alchemy and Jewelcrafting skill trees and combined into Sanctified Oil, which comes in four tiers, ranging from +50 to +125 points of Item Power boost. The oil can be applied to any item with Item Power to boost its stats permanently.[/p][/*][*][p]Added the ability to craft Founders' rewards in the Log Workbench, located near every Petra Dei. It complements the still available method of using the Founders Crafting Table to craft those recipes.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the same tier of potions with different durations would wildly and unexpectedly vary in value provided. Now it is standardized with slight variation based on tier.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now craft a total of 36 new RP wearables, with no stats. The selection includes capes, hats, dresses, tunics, pants, shoes, and new diadems.[/p][/*][*][p]Deer bucks now drop antlers as a guaranteed drop. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Building[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The building integrity values of the low foundation pieces were fixed to give more support.[/p][/*][*][p]The building integrity of some smaller foundation pieces was fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]Two Granite foundation pieces now cost 5 instead of 10 granite to better align with the piece size.[/p][/*][*][p]All Plots owned by characters in a specific Server Region are now shown to the Player.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed snapping point on Balustrade, Limestone pieces.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed snap-point selection for several small objects.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the amount of Granite needed to build low walls.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now set permissions to sell items at your market stall to Public.  [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Revamped Lobby and Character Creator[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Created a new lobby for the game to make it fit better into the style of the game.[/p][/*][*][p]The new lobby includes a short set of introduction screens to Pax Dei. notes.title: PvP System Changes: Everything You Need to Know
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello Paxians,[/h2][p][/p][p]We’re excited to introduce the big changes that will be coming to PvP in Pax Dei, starting with Verse 4! Whether you’re a seasoned fighter or just dipping your toes into the world of player combat, here’s everything you need to know about the [b]reworked PvP system[/b]: what’s changing, what’s staying, and how you can prepare. All the details and concepts below are still a work in progress, and we’re eager to get your feedback and suggestions to improve them and ensure they suit your gameplay style.[/p][p]Before we go into details, let’s first talk about where we are and what we aim to achieve.[/p][p]We know some players hate PvP, some love it and others are in between - if the reward is worth the risk, they’ll do it, but the reward really has to be there and the risk has to be understood. As such, we still think PvP in Pax Dei should be a choice and players should have the ability to opt in, whether that’s through joining a PvP alliance or travelling to a PvP-enabled area in the game.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/c7fba4e2837c2b1e76d6dfefb28abd33a288a4d9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This brings us to Pax Dei: the peace of the divine mechanic that controls where PvP is available. At the time of writing this blog, the Home Valleys and the Wildlands are protected under Pax Dei and players are safe from PvP mechanics, while Lyonesse is a PvP-enabled forsaken area with no protection. You, as a player, have no control over this… yet. Our goal is to gradually change this over time, introducing elements that make the game more challenging in certain areas while giving you control of Pax Dei through specific mechanics.[/p][p]The role of PvP in Pax Dei is multi-fold. We want to see the PvP systems result in large alliances being formed, castles being built, and drama unfolding in the field of war and politics, with spies, backstabbing and bribery. Getting to the top leadership positions should be hard work - but also attainable with cunning. A ruler leading the largest army in the game should never have to step on the field of battle if they and their subjects so choose. It’ll take time, but each update will take us closer to this vision.[/p][p]We also want to create systems that allow competition - and create tension - along multiple axes of the game, not just PvP. Some players should be able to exert physical power, while a rich merchant should be able to use their gold for power.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8bbc12d890f437dd306479e9e3ffc2677a588fa9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]All of this will result in a game where we hope to see a healthy player-driven economy, where the competition will lead into destruction and demand of goods, enabling those who love the crafting parts of the game to meaningfully participate and feel their work is appreciated. So while this document will detail elements some of you will not want to participate in, our goal is to make a better game for you all.[/p][p]Let’s jump into a bit more detail on what we’re thinking.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/5cac568f33dd272295ae90f23796a614a1d4f7e3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Phase 1 - Verse 4[/h2][p]Lyonesse is becoming much larger. The updated Lyonesse is a full-blown 10x10 km area with 5 zones. Four of the zones are in the corners and contain entry portals, with a central zone in the middle, accessible from all four corners. Each area has PvE sites, with the center being significantly more dangerous than the other areas.[/p][p]The four corner areas all have a Petra Dei inside them, with a Pax Dei protected area surrounding the Petra Dei. The Petra Dei has all the services you expect, with crafters and storage.[/p][p]The thinking behind making Lyonesse larger is, as you’ll read below, that there’s a ton of gameplay we’ll be introducing to Lyonesse in subsequent updates, and this requires space. We’ve looked at the extraction gameplay in Lyonesse and with the gameplay that’s landing, the larger area was also warranted to allow players to dip in and out with significant PvP risk - but no guarantee of getting caught each time.[/p][p]Lyonesse now comes with two new resources only found in the area. Ambergrasp and Canonite are refined using Alchemy and Jewelcrafting and will allow creation of Sanctified Oil, which can be used to Enchant any gear with Item Power, with up to a 125-point boost to the Item Power of the Enchanted item. The enchantment is permanent when applied to the item. The resources can be found on the ground, but are predominantly found as loot on NPCs in the area, and the most lucrative drops will be on NPCs in the central area of Lyonesse.[/p][p]The goal of this update is to prepare for the future, but also give you a good reason to venture into Lyonesse in search of riches.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/677d8673873a7b0b3d94aa96cc2ac59f4330ffa6.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/717aedcd1994c3f78047d801794eba5ebc3e62d9.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/1fa00d0f254be353cd891b77df5105c3d1f5d5d9.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Phase 2[/h2][p]While Heartlands in Pax Dei will be sacrosanct and will not be wiped after the game launch, Lyonesse will feature seasons. The rules and gameplay will change in Lyonesse between the seasons, and the first one will likely last 6 months.[/p][p]The PvP update after Verse 4 will introduce a new mechanism where clans will be able to claim a piece of land in Lyonesse and place plots in the area they’ve claimed. The plots will allow building exactly as if you were in Heartlands, with the distinction that the plot placement is only available to the members of the clan.[/p][p]The number of spots that can be claimed will be limited. To capture a spot, the clans will have to have access to a new resource to pay for the claim - and upkeep - for the ownership. The resource will be constrained in availability, and clans who want to own land in Lyonesse will be either trading or fighting to get access to it.[/p][p]Having land in Lyonesse will have huge benefits, bringing safety, storage and crafting to the clan. The claimed spot is likely to act as a respawn shrine for the clan in control of the site, so being in control of a spot next to a good PvE site will be extremely beneficial.[/p][p]We are looking at improving some plot-level permissions as part of this work to facilitate creation of safe fortresses.[/p][p]We’re also looking at changing the rules related to death and property. Right now, Pax Dei forces the same rules everywhere across the game world, and the need for corpse runs feels very harsh in the Heartlands. We don’t have final details yet, but it’s likely that going forward you no longer have to make a corpse run after respawning in a Shrine in Home Valleys, but also we’ll likely add a small chance for some stackable items being destroyed and will tune the death damage to any gear with health.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/d2878f124a8bf30ed65e0adb61159154238b7166.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]After phase 2[/h2][p]The following features are in the design phase, so the timing, order and exact design might still change, but we wanted to give you a glimpse of where the game is going.[/p][p][b]Feudal Houses [/b]will allow a Clan to flag itself as a Feudal House, with the Clan leader becoming a Knight. Knights can swear fealty to each other, thus forming a larger alliance, which will affect the PvP flagging of all players in the alliance. We will likely require that the land in Lyonesse can only be controlled by Houses. [/p][p]Houses are likely to get the means to claim areas outside of Lyonesse as their sphere of influence and gain benefits such as taxation rights in these areas. However, doing this will open the alliance up to war declarations, with the alliance being flagged for PvP also outside of Lyonesse when at war.[/p][p][b]Market Towns[/b] will change the areas around the Petra Deis in Lyonesse. The areas will stay as safe harbors inside Lyonesse and feature plots that allow building. Where the plots elsewhere in Lyonesse require combat for ownership, the plots in the Market Towns will use economic competition and you will be bidding gold against other players for control of these plots. We’re looking at making these areas central trading hubs and are likely to make changes related to speed travel and resource transportation as the towns come online, but don’t have exact details to share on that yet.[/p][p][b]Parishes[/b] will allow players to form an alliance to enable a Priest to collect large amounts of Grace. We’re looking at enabling the Priest to not only cast new very expensive Miracles, but also to control Pax Dei with Altars, securing claimed sites in Lyonesse from PvP. We’re also looking at new Positions of Power, where priests can anoint members of the Feudal Houses into new positions.[/p][p][/p][h2]Get Ready for the New PvP Era[/h2][p]As you can imagine, these updates require quite a lot of work, changes, additions and adjustments, and not everything will be released all at once.[/p][p]The new era for Pax Dei PvP will start with the new Lyonesse and Enchanting. Following this, we’ll add building in Lyonesse, with more to follow.[/p][p]Please provide your feedback on Discord, in the [url="https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1410957277229219900/1410957277229219900"]dedicated thread[/url].[/p][p]Whether you’re looking to dominate the battlefield, build an economic empire in a Market Town, or just survive in the wilds, there’ll be something for every PvP player with these changes.[/p][p]The real fight for Lyonesse will soon begin! 🔥[/p][p]Bellum vobiscum, 
The Mainframe Team [/p]

notes.title: UI & Item icons - Upcoming update
notes.notes:
[p]Hello Paxians,[/p][p]We wanted to share with you some work in progress our team is doing regarding icons and UI in general. [/p][p][/p][h2]Items Icons[/h2][p]We’re excited to share that our team is working on an update for the item icons! We know that the recently added icons haven’t been as clear as we’d like, which can sometimes cause confusion. That’s why we’re introducing a more visually intuitive system, making it easier to instantly recognize both the quality level and tier of an item at a glance.[/p][p]The concept below is still a work in progress, but the final result should look quite similar. Bonus: you’ll also catch a sneak peek at the Mastercrafting system mentioned in Tuesday’s news and [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WEvYuISwCxI"]interview[/url].[/p][p][/p][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/4120041f1328edfcf2e329eef2995781c73a5e07.png"][/img]
UI Update[/h2][p]Our UI team is also hard at work on unifying the game’s interface. In short, our focal points are essentially to make your experience more consistent, making sure the UI doesn’t get in the way anymore, and allowing our UI’s to be more predictable and scalable. 

To actually show you, instead of writing promising words that might feel empty, we’ve included a bunch of images. Keep in mind though, that these images are a work in progress outline for the design, and their looks will be updated to fit in better stylistically with the medieval setting of Pax Dei. 

We’re aiming to make our in-game main menus, like our Inventory, Crafting menu, Character menu (currently equipment), Clan Menu, Markets, and Grace, follow the standard of our latest Journal update. So we’re gradually moving to a more docked panel on the right side of the screen, moving the UI more out of the way so you can focus on the world of Pax Dei and its gameplay. Identical to the latest Journal update, we’re also moving the details of the focused item into a floating tooltip. Aside from these bigger, more visually apparent changes, we’re also updating all of the keybind inputs along the way to make sure that the UI of the menus no longer conflict with the inputs that you need for combat and other gameplay-related features.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/1bfe11a1c9b32c6dfb93b3a49fb46c2ce45f29c1.png"][/img][img The enemies with a skull (intended for parties) still give more XP overall when engaged in a party.[/p][/*][*][p]Harvesting skills now give XP based on the damage caused as a % of the total health of the tree/mineable/carcass being processed, so tools that cause more damage give more XP / XP event. With the earlier balance, using better tools in some cases was reducing the total XP earned due to chopping/skinning/mining faster and this no longer happens.[/p][/*][*][p]The XP earned in mining, woodchopping, and skinning has been re-balanced to match the new level requirements, so the total amount of actions needed to reach the skill cap has been reduced significantly compared to earlier balances.[/p][/*][*][p]Note: XP progression of the harvesting skills is not currently popping in the HUD when harvesting.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Carpentry Progression[/b][/h3][list][*][p]We recognized that progression in the Carpentry skill, particularly at higher levels, currently feels too restrictive. [b]35[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]All level [b]39 unlocks[/b] have been moved down to [b]level 30[/b].[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]These changes should help ease the bottleneck while we work on a broader rebalancing.[/p][h3][b]Other[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Damage to shields from blocking has been reduced by 75%.[/p][/*][*][p]Inquisitor Captain’s Rallying Cry damage buff has been reduced by effect has been adjusted.[/p][/*][*][p]The Aura of Life VFX no longer sticks forever when double-activated.[/p][/*][*][p]A keybind field was added to the settings/keybinds menu to allow players to hide the UI.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a number of recipe unlocks that we overlooked when we simplified unlocking requirements to either rely on skill level or key ingredient discovery (not both).[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where HP were not granted adequately upon respawn after death.[/p][/*][*][p]Some item descriptions have been fixed to show correct data instead of a {} notes.title: Hotfix - 18/6/2025
notes.notes: [h2]Combat XP[/h2][list][*][p]The combat skill XP requirements and ranges of XP earned for enemies have been comprehensively revamped. The XP for a Tier 1 base level enemy is now 100 XP, with other enemies scaling this number up or down based on the enemy tier and rank. The resulting combat XP requirements are now very close to the crafting skills.[/p][/*][*][p]The XP gained from hard-to-kill enemies has been increased relative to the easier-to-kill enemies. The XP requirements to level up have been adjusted, so it’s highly beneficial to group up and hunt for harder-to-kill enemies instead of grinding easy kills in Heartlands. With the combination of the two, there’s no more effort to level up to the skill cap if you solely kill easy enemies and less effort if you group up and go after the hard enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]XP earned when in parties has been tuned. Enemies intended for soloing now distribute the XP across the party in a manner where the total XP earned by the party is the same as if you were soloing the enemy. Enemies intended for parties now give an increasing amount of total XP based on the party size, for up to 3.3x their base XP for a party of 6, so the most effective way to level up should always be to party up.[/p][/*][*][p]XP gained from animals has been significantly increased to make it easier to level up combat skills related to hunting.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug related to some enemies giving 0 XP.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug related some enemies giving more XP.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Spells / Weapons[/h2][list][*][p]Bow damage has been increased across all tiers.[/p][list][*][p]The arrows provide a stronger progression on damage.[/p][/*][*][p]Bow damage has been increased throughout the whole itempower range.[/p][/*][*][p]The bow handling and draw speed increases faster with itempower.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue that caused Aura of Life spell to cause lingering particle effects and performance drop[/p][/*][*][p]Breath of Joy I & II, Surging Stride and Spirit Stride now do not interrupt autorunning once activated.[/p][/*][*][p]Quiet stand and Sanctified Stance now handle their cooldown properly, consistent with the item slot they are in. They also now correctly forces the other one on cooldown when attempted to overlap their activations.[/p][/*][*][p]Fix for Divine Intervention applying both the <40% heal and normal heal when it was applied.[/p][/*][*][p]Divine shield now only reflects damage up to a maximum value described in the spell's description[/p][/*][*][p]Greatsword weapon special "Guardbreaker" now properly forces a block break in PvP[/p][/*][*][p]Killmark spell now correctly grants movement speed when the target is killed.[/p][/*][*][p]Sacrament of Strife healing provided appropriately scales with ItemPower.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some status effects were not removed with cleanse or revoke.[/p][/*][*][p]Windlash now correctly shows the duration of the chained status.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with Jester's Flask spell disappearing when throwing at other characters.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed revoke not removing divine rapture stacks from the target.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed for all non damaging spell projectiles doing damage based on the wieldable damage[/p][/*][/list][h2]Gathering[/h2][list][*][p]Hold to interact resource gathering will now correctly re-equip offhand wieldables upon completion.[/p][/*][*][p]Resource node hardness value now matches the tool's tier required to gather it. (0-4)[/p][/*][*][p]Gathering tool damage progression was rebalanced, significantly increasing the tool damage across the whole range.[/p][/*][*][p]Skinning hardness of wolves were increased to 1 (in the new range).[/p][/*][*][p]Skinning health was rebalanced for all skinnable animals[/p][/*][/list][h2]Audio[/h2][list][*][p]Fixed audio from Water wells being too loud.[/p][/*][*][p]Polished audio for sitting animations.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with Tempest Command not playing its chain sound on bound enemies.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Crafting[/h2][list][*][p]Recipe List refresh on level up.[/p][list][*][p]When you gain a profession level while crafting and you unlock new recipes, the recipe list now automatically refreshes and you no longer need to manually reopen the crafter.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Crafting Time Reduction[/p][list][*][p]Crafting timers were very excessive (especially when crafting gear). We've reduced these timers substantially or by roughly 1/2. We will continue to monitor feedback regarding them for future refining of the system.[/p][/*][*][p]Gear should now take 9-12 rolls to craft, based on recipe complexity (down from a whooping 21 roll afk coffee break).[/p][/*][*][p]Once fully Mastered, these crafts should only require you 3-4 rolls.[/p][/*][*][p]Other non-gear recipes should also be slightly faster.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Recipe Unlock Progression[/p][list][*][p]Many crafting stations — particularly processing crafters — previously had unclear progression paths that often left players confused or blocked. It wasn’t always obvious what each station was for or how to progress in the associated profession, largely due to missing or hidden recipes.[/p][list][*][p]To improve this, we’ve made recipe progression more transparent: more recipes are now unlocked by default, and key recipes that were previously gated behind obscure item requirements now unlock through skill progression instead.[/p][/*][*][p]These changes affect many crafters including Spinning Wheels, Looms, Tanning Racks, Charcoal Kilns, Pottery Kilns, Furnaces, Tailoring Tables and Leatherworking Tables.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]More crafting stations unlocked by default[/p][list][*][p]We wanted to smoothen out some basic progression discovery at the start and therefore the [b]Founder’s Crafting Table, Basic Charcoal Kiln, the Log Workbench and the Basic Furnace are now all unlocked by default[/b] in the build menu.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Furnace Parts[/p][list][*][p]Many of you reported that they couldn't find the recipe for Furnace Parts [i]Sorry!![/i]. The recipe can now be found in the Basic Forge, as it should :)[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Steel Anvil and other unintended items[/p][list][*][p]Quite a few items accidentally made it into the game in the latest creation, same with recipes or items visible in the Journal that shouldn't have. A lot of these were either deprecated items or placeholder items that may or may not be part of future content releases. They've now been properly removed. Example: Steel Anvil.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Nightshade Fruit[/p][list][*][p]A recipe for the T2 Alchemy Workbench mistakenly called for a “Deadly Nightshade Fruit” — which, tragically, did not exist. It now correctly asks for Nightshade Fruit. Please note: we still do not recommend eating it. Side effects may include confusion, nausea, alchemical mishaps, and/or death.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Crafting Blessings at max level[/p][list][*][p]When using a profession blessing at level 40 takes you to level 41 but it didn’t effectively increase your skill beyond 40. Now it will! [/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]Other[/b][/h2][list][*][p]Fixed an issue in the Construction hammer UI where "Claim a plot to start building crafters" in German and French exceeded its designated space[/p][/*][*][p]Updated localization in several instances.[/p][/*][*][p]Clay now spawns in greater density around water, in addition to new spawn locations near cliffs.[/p][/*][*][p]Hunters have discovered a breakthrough in animal carcass logistics. You can now pile up 20 of them.[/p][/*][*][p]Game no longer switches to walk mode when opening inventory while stationary or when interacting with crafters.[/p][/*][*][p]Spirit regain floating text numbers are now only visible to the user.[/p][/*][*][p]Healing floating text numbers are scaled down when targets are at full health.[/p][/*][*][p]Arrow recipes (in the crafting menu) now show the intended item description.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where swapping equipped items which share the same base granted spell would lose the ability to determine the granting item (and thus their ItemPower) causing them to fall back to minimum stats.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed sprint players being able to sprint without consuming stamina after passing zone boundary[/p][/*][*][p]The gold amount shown in the top bar and in your inventory will now consistently show you the correct amount.[/p][/*][*][p]You can no longer open the Redeeming Queue and Redeem items while dead.[/p][/*][*][p]Consumables now correctly show the cooldown of it instead of the duration of its effect.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some world areas close to the the Province edges that had an unintended non-blocking landscape mesh.[/p][/*][*][p]Teleporting while wielding a hammer no longer results in an extra cylinder in game view.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][b]Patch Notes - Hotfix - 17/6/2025,[/b][/h1][list][*][p]Fixed an issue to address various server crashes.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Path of the Adventurer - Patch Notes
notes.notes: [p]This update significantly changes core systems, world structure, and gameplay flow. Verse 3 lays the foundation for a richer, more immersive journey.[/p][previewyoutube="QymybCFt_Oo;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Please note that [b]we anticipate an 8-hour maintenance window on June 11, starting at 8:30 a.m. UTC,[/b] during which the servers will be unavailable. [/p][h2][b]New Features[/b][/h2][h3][b]World[/b][/h3][p]The world has been resculpted, with an increased maximum number of plots per Province. Changes include:[/p][list][*][p]Ten Home Valleys per Province (instead of six).[/p][/*][*][p]Smaller but more engaging Wildlands.[/p][/*][*][p]Merrie and Kerys Provinces have swapped their positions.[/p][/*][*][p]Biome distribution and enemy camp placements have been adjusted worldwide.[/p][/*][*][p]Petra Dei sites revamp with starting crafters.[/p][/*][*][p]Some crafting sites have been added to the world.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Building/Crafting[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Several professions have been reviewed to fit the RPG changes and to make the onboarding easier, the progression smoother, and the dependencies smarter.[/p][/*][*][p]New starting crafter: the Log Workbench. The Carpenter's Workbench is now dedicated to Furnishing pieces.[/p][/*][*][p]The 'chamois goat' (aka wild goat) was added in mountainous areas, which provides wool.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Profession: Skinning[/b][/p][list][*][p]Skinning knives with new skinning skill requirements.[/p][/*][*][p]Can be used on dead creatures to extract valuable components for crafting.[/p][/*][*][p]Dead creatures respect the existing rules for looting permission.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Several new building pieces have been added to the game: a Granite Foundations set, a Limestone set, a Log set, and more.[/p][/*][*][p]A hunter-themed Market Stall variant has been added to the game.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2][b]Gameplay[/b][/h2][h3][b]Combat Skill Progression[/b]:[/h3][list][*][p]We introduced new combat skills reflecting your affinity with armor slots: six skills (head, chest, legs, feet, arms, and hands) per armor strength (Heavy, Medium, Light), so eighteen in total.[/p][/*][*][p]Combat XP comes from killing enemies and now contributes to leveling specific weapon/armor skills.[/p][/*][*][p]Combat XP gains now appear as floating numbers near your character, similar to damage indicators.[/p][/*][*][p]Killing harder enemies generally means they grant more experience.[/p][/*][*][p]Party Experience is shared with all members in proximity.[/p][/*][*][p]Party Experience shares experience depending on the type of enemy killed:[/p][list][*][p]Veteran enemies (shown by a skull icon in their nameplate) are meant for full parties.[/p][/*][*][p]Normal enemies are meant for solo or small groups.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]Blocking[/b][/h3][list][*][p]One-handed weapons can no longer block (without holding a shield)[/p][/*][*][p]Improved responsiveness of blocking in certain situations[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]New Gear and Weapons[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Reduced the number of equipment slots: we reduced the number of slots specifically in areas where all armor types didn't have an item available in those slots.[/p][/*][*][p]The following slots are now combined:[/p][list][*][p]Top, Top-Outer and Shoulder slots were changed to a combined Top slot.[/p][/*][*][p]Bottom and Bottom-outer slots were changed to a combined Bottom slot.[/p][/*][*][p]Armor roles are defined using new attributes with these themes:[/p][list][*][p]Heavy armor has the best physical resistances and the least damage. Additionally, it grants the user with bonus threat generation and crowd control efficiency.[/p][/*][*][p]Medium Armor has average survivability and decent damage output. Making it an ideal choice for physical damage dealers.[/p][/*][*][p]Light armor (clothing) has the best magical resistances and the best damage but the worst physical defense values. Additionally, it gains bonuses to healing.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Each armor item in the Head/Chest/Legs/Feet slots has a spell, even for common crafted items:[/p][list][*][p]Heavy armor offers spells primarily for the tank role.[/p][/*][*][p]Medium armor class offers spells primarily for physical damage dealers.[/p][/*][*][p]Light armor class offers spells primarily for healers and spellcasters.[/p][/*][*][p]It is expected that players will be mixing and matching different armor classes for certain attribute setups and spell combinations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]Item power[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Items now have minimum skill requirements to use; if the player does not meet these requirements they will get a notification about not having enough skill to use.[/p][/*][*][p]Item power scales items and spells:[/p][list][*][p]All weapons and gear are now defined with an Item Power, which is used to describe their basic attributes. This helps differentiate Tier levels for gear, while providing more visible, granular gains as players level up the skills associated with their favorite gear and weapons.[/p][/*][*][p]Item quality and Tier level influence the gear’s base Item Power.[/p][/*][*][p]Character skill level further influences the Item Power, further increasing the base stats of those items, and the abilities they grant.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]New spells on Armor items[/b][/h3][p]List of spells per wearable[/p][list][*][p][b]Heavy Helm[/b][/p][list][*][p]Mental Fortitude[/p][list][*][p]Makes you [b]immune to displacement[/b] effects and increases your crowd control resistance by [b]25[/b] for [b]20s[/b].[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Quick Remedy[/p][list][*][p]Increases healing received by [b]25%[/b] for [b]10[/b] seconds. notes.title: Spotlight - Upcoming Crafting Changes
notes.notes:
Hello Paxians,

As we continue reshaping Pax Dei’s core systems, crafting is stepping into the spotlight. With the arrival of [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i], we’re not just adding new recipes or tweaking numbers: we’re rethinking the entire structure and flow of crafting to make it more engaging, intuitive, and meaningful at every tier.

This revamp is major. It complements the updates to combat and progression, and it reflects months of work by the design team to better align the system with how players actually want to play: more meaningful gathering, more strategic crafting, and clearer professional identities.

[i]Disclaimer: it’s possible that, by the time the update is deployed, some minor changes will occur to the details below. [/i]

[h2]Four Key Goals[/h2]

We’ve structured the crafting overhaul around four core design goals:

[h3]Easier Onboarding[/h3]

One of the most common points of feedback from players, especially newer ones, has been that starting a crafting profession feels unclear or overly dependent on other players. We're addressing that by:
[list]
[*] Making it faster and simpler to start any core profession,
[*] Removing the need for a dedicated processing crafter to begin basic crafting,
[*] Streamlining the early game to help you get into the loop quickly without getting stuck on bottlenecks.
[/list]
This lowers the barrier to entry and makes early progression more rewarding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/de4cb2fa2fc42b6c6a80a0a5b2b772d8cac51dfe.png[/img]

[h3]Real Complexity, Not Confusion[/h3]

Crafting should grow deeper as you master it, not just more time-consuming. We're adding real structure and logical depth to recipes across tiers:
[list]
[*] Tiered complexity: T1 recipes remain simple, but higher tiers introduce more layered ingredient chains.
[*] Cross-profession clarity: Components will now more clearly belong to your profession or to another, reducing ambiguity.
[*] Persistent value: Early-tier items, especially Tier 1, will retain relevance at higher tiers  (e.g., as ingredients or in alternate recipes)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/3d2efe92401c8f9d3b92201b1b7303b87e0df882.jpg[/img]
[h3]Smarter Dependencies[/h3]

Crafting collaboration is good, but dependencies shouldn’t be frustrating. We’re restructuring how professions rely on each other:
[list]
[*] Components from other professions will now be at least one tier lower than the item being crafted,
[*] This preserves interdependence while avoiding deadlocks and confusion,
[*] It also helps reduce crafting overhead when you’re focused on progressing in your own field.
[/list]
This change keeps specialization valuable without punishing solo crafters or small groups.

[h3]Better Pacing[/h3]

We want crafting to be more about the world, and less about waiting at a bench.
[list]
[*] Progress and costs are being balanced across all three core professions,
[*] We’re increasing the importance of gathering and reducing the need to be idle at crafting stations,
[*] Changes include adjusted yields, ingredient costs, and XP multipliers to reflect this philosophy.
[/list]
This means that your time in the world — gathering, hunting, mining — is what drives your progress, not just standing still and watching a progress bar.

[h2]What’s New in the Toolbox[/h2]

This revamp comes with new workflows, new materials, and ultimately, new gear. Here are some highlights:

[h3]New workflow[/h3]

As we introduced in our recent post on RPG, the crafting changes are designed to support and enhance the new combat system. That’s why tailoring, leatherworking and Blacksmithing are the three professions undergoing drastic changes, as they are the ones used to craft gear and weapons. 
[list]
[*] New spells and gear stats require new crafting inputs,
[*] Combat roles like Tank, DPS, and Healer are now reflected in the gear you craft,
[*] Reworked recipes will provide tactical choices for builders, gatherers, and fighters alike.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/39432046113098f82291275a75d3a7dbf2c05824.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8a3d6441b0438ffc4bd13c371b1dd4b29e4d4e1b.png[/img]

[h3]New Crafting Components[/h3]

Most professions are gaining a full suite of new intermediate material, designed to support the new tiered structure. These parts will appear at different tiers and will help distinguish recipes by complexity and function.

For example, leatherworkers will now work with a new intermediary material: Leather Splits, available in various qualities. This gives more control over final item quality and adds depth to leatherworking progression.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/9e72ccad3f697c79479db12de68a415c13447a5a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/9e08b7568e2ab02cdecabdfed62dc9076a971b64.png[/img]

[h3]New Items Replacing Old Gear[/h3]

Almost all existing crafted gear, including weapons, will be phased out and replaced with newly designed items that better match the revamped progression and balance systems.

If you’ve been hoarding mats for that perfect build, keep an eye on the new crafting tables — what’s viable and valuable is about to change significantly.

Crafting is one of the core pillars of Pax Dei, and this update is a long-overdue leap forward. It makes the system more intuitive, rewarding, and integrated with the rest of the game. Overall, progressing in a profession should be more rewarding; the higher the craft, the better the value. However, higher crafts will require more materials, so more time wandering the world - or quite some gold to buy those at a market stall.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/80a5c42181d071750f38778a134c16dee7c601f0.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/064e26ab6107eef99d21edd2c94724117bb7bc07.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/064e26ab6107eef99d21edd2c94724117bb7bc07.png[/img]
Whether you're just picking up your first tool or running a full workshop, we can’t wait to see what you build next.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

Verse 3 brings a major transformation to the world of Pax Dei: reshaping the land, streamlining exploration, and getting players closer together than ever before. From social-focused design changes to structural foundations for future features, here’s what awaits you in [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i].

[h2]More Heartlands, Closer Communities[/h2]

The number of Heartlands, aka the home valleys, has increased from 6 to 10 per Province, as seen on the [url=https://playpaxdei.com/media/player-resources]newly updated maps[/url]. These valleys are now [b]smaller and more numerous[/b], and the reasons behind this change are both practical and social:
[list]
[*] [b]Higher player density[/b]: You’ll now encounter other players more often, making the Heartlands feel livelier.
[*][b] Stronger local communities[/b]: Tighter spaces foster more natural cooperation, trade, and neighborhood-building.
[*] [b]Smarter Wildlands[/b]: Previously vast and often empty, the Wilds have been slightly reduced in size to concentrate activity, encourage encounters, and make exploration more meaningful.
[*] [b]Improved balance[/b]: Biome distribution and enemy camp placement have been adjusted across the world to ensure a smoother progression and more thematic consistency. The enemy camp’s density has also increased significantly, both in the Home Valleys and the Wildlands.
[*] [b]Scalability[/b]: With more Heartlands per Shard, the world can now accommodate a growing player base without fragmenting the community.
[/list]
This marks one of our boldest steps yet toward a more dynamic, interconnected world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/1a9d8229c668b9a28e121013753ad416d1638ba7.jpg[/img]
[h2]A Living, Breathing World[/h2]

The world of [i]Pax Dei[/i] has never felt more alive or more mysterious.

Across every valley and ridge, you’ll discover [b]new sites and visual upgrades[/b] that elevate the landscape and deepen immersion:

[list]
[*][b] Revamped stone circles[/b], each with unique architecture and a stronger sense of history.
[*] [b]Rebuilt Petra Dei starting zones[/b], reimagined as ancient sanctuaries turned base camps, complete with warmth, crafting stations, and space to welcome new and future ‘plotless’ players.
[*] [b]Adding crafting sites[/b], expanding settlement strategies, and crafting hubs. On top of the revamped Petra Dei sites, we added some small crafting sites with public crafting stations in the Home Valleys and the Wildlands.
[/list]
And if you're paying attention, you'll notice [b]sealed cave entrances, foundations for future town sites[/b], and [b]ominous Inquisitor Citadels[/b] on the horizon, silent promises of stories yet to unfold.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/2e8adda76668165fd4d759fcdfa479890ada23db.jpg[/img]
The natural world has evolved too:
[list]
[*] [b]Forests are thicker[/b], richer in atmosphere and detail.
[*] [b]The Corrupted Planes twist with strange new growths.[/b]
[*] Regions like the [b]Scrublands, Whispering Woods, and Cursed Rockland[/b] have been refreshed with deeper textures and moodier biomes.
[*] [b]Grass and trees sway with the wind:[/b] we made some improvements to limit motion sickness while keeping the atmosphere vivid.
[*] [b]Ancient Stelae[/b] are now more naturally embedded in the terrain, enriching lore and immersion.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/20b935438fe7ae3ecb9971ee0dc71b72b51a7cb0.jpg[/img]
To complement the visual upgrades, the terrain itself is now more welcoming:
[list]
[*] [b]Fewer steep cliffs[/b], smoother [b]travel routes[/b], and improved [b]road intersections[/b] mean easier, more enjoyable navigation.
[*] [b]Backdrop mountains and snowlines[/b] have been fine-tuned for visual coherence.
[*] [b]Small ponds[/b] now dot the countryside, adding charm and diversity.
[*] And though the world retains its rolling hills, [b]foundation pieces make it easier than ever to build on any terrain[/b].
[/list]
[h2]A Not-So-Subtle Map Shift[/h2]

If you're a seasoned traveler in Pax Dei, you might notice something... off. That’s because [b]Kerys and Merrie have swapped places on the map[/b].

This wasn’t part of a grand redesign plan, rather, a practical adjustment driven by [b]some upcoming needs tied to Verse 4[/b]. We needed to create a bit more room near the Lyonesse gates, and this reorganization turned out to be the simplest way to make it happen.

We understand this may feel disorienting at first, especially for veteran players. But we hope the long-term benefits will make it worth the adjustment.

[h2]Polish, Performance, and Promise[/h2]

Behind the scenes, the world’s streaming systems have been upgraded for [b]better performance and faster asset loading[/b]. Countless floating objects, terrain glitches, and visual oddities have also been cleaned up to provide a more polished and consistent experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/49fcea1b4d1f8ec94872880ba00cc307ac456dd1.jpg[/img]
Together, these changes bring a world that feels more cohesive, more believable, and more ready for the adventures to come.

We hope you're as excited as we are to set foot in this revitalized world when [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i] launches.

Stay tuned for upcoming deep dives into the [b]RPG system overhaul and crafting evolution[/b].

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Migration Update: Upgrading from Amazon RDS Postgres to Amazon Aurora
notes.notes:
Hello Paxians,

We know some of you are eager to learn what’s happening on the backend. Today, we’d like to shed some light on the recent changes we made to our database, why we made the upgrade and the consequences for Pax Dei.

[h2]Overview[/h2]
To improve the reliability and scalability of our system, we recently migrated from our legacy Amazon RDS Postgres system to Amazon Aurora (Postgres compatible). This migration required us to schedule two maintenance breaks to make necessary database changes with a double goal.

[list]
[*] Enhanced Reliability:
[list]
[*] Our previous setup with Amazon RDS Postgres, which used a primary and a secondary node, offered a reliable setup where the secondary node can take over and be promoted to a master node in the case of a failure. This failover worked well but could result in several minutes of downtime during the switch.
[*] Aurora databases have a shared, reliable storage layer between all nodes, which 
significantly reduces recovery time from minutes to seconds by offering rapid failover from a primary to a secondary node.
[*] Aurora also allows us to dynamically add and remove additional nodes from the database cluster.
[/list]
[*] Improved Scalability:
[list]
[*] The old system required significant downtime to implement changes - as any major changes require us to use the failover mechanisms between nodes while performing upgrades or changes to each.
[*] Aurora provides the flexibility to scale resources up or down and adjust database node sizes with minimal disruption.
[/list]
[/list]
With the migration to Amazon Aurora now complete, we now have a better uptime and enhanced reliability with faster failover, as well as seamless scalability to support future growth. 

This migration positions us to better serve you, our community, by providing a more robust and flexible database infrastructure.

Stay tuned for more insights on Pax Dei development!
Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: The Road Ahead – March Update
notes.notes:
Hello Paxians,

Since the beginning of Early Access, Pax Dei has been a journey shaped by you — our passionate players. As we reflect on the progress we’ve made and the path ahead, we want to be transparent about the challenges we’ve faced, priorities we’ve had to adjust, and our ongoing commitment to building a game that thrives on meaningful player interactions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8933d815aa4eb4f27e94477c58063d4b48f9ee23.jpg[/img]
[h2]Reflecting on Early Access[/h2]
The main goal for us moving into Early Access was to get constant feedback from a live community to help us develop the game. And wow, did the community deliver!

We’re grateful for, and humbled by, your continuous engagement. Over 70,000 of you are following Pax Dei’s development journey on our official Discord, and sharing tips and tricks daily to help other players.  

Looking at the different parts of the game, here is where we stand today. We spent the first months stabilizing the game. Then, our first update, [i][b]Proving Grounds[/b][/i], was about addressing some of the biggest challenges we saw emerging before we could focus on adding new systems to deepen the game with [i][b]Market Square[/b][/i] onwards.

We also had to make tough decisions. Some features we initially planned had to be deprioritized as we focused on strengthening the foundations of Pax Dei.

While this meant delays in some areas, like the highly expected PvP system or the Knight/Soldier feature, it has also allowed us to deploy some elements sooner than planned in the roadmap — and even to add new elements that will make Pax Dei stronger in the long run.

[h2]Early game [/h2]
The first obvious lesson from Early Access was that it took too long to get to the fun at the first contact with the game. Part of [i][b]Proving Grounds[/b][/i] was about addressing this: we placed enemy camps in the Heartland valleys and added basic gear and spells so that players now have the option to go on an adventure within the first few hours of play.

The introduction of the Journal, along with an overall balancing pass, also helped make the learning curve for crafting less steep.

And talking about adventure, the world revamp also included our first new biome since Alpha, the Corrupted Plains. More recently, the addition of the Compass makes finding your way around the world of Pax Dei more convenient.

We’re far from done with this aspect of the game and intend to keep iterating on it in upcoming content updates.

[h2]Combat[/h2]
Combat remains a major focus. In [i][b]Proving Grounds[/b][/i], we reworked the animation and player movement systems to improve the sec-to-sec combat experience, making it feel smoother and more responsive, while also laying a stronger foundation for future improvements.

We also added new spells, rebalanced gear, and gave the Inquisitors and Lost Souls a full rework.

In its current form, however, combat often lacks meaningful decision-making. We aim to move to a state where your gear choices and abilities will shape your tactics, encouraging you to build specialized roles.

This will be the central part of our next Verse. Check below for a sneak peek, and we look forward to sharing more soon.

[h2]Building[/h2]
Building is undoubtedly the most complete system in the game. We’re amazed at how it unlocks the creativity of the community. Watching the world fill up with beautiful villages, mighty fortresses, and sprawling cities is a constant joy.

We’ve been regularly adding new pieces to the game and plan on expanding the building sets to give even more options to our master builders. Yes, the highly expected Limestone should be part of Verse 3!

That said, the free-form nature of our building system comes with a number of challenges, notably on the performance side.The valleys with the most spectacular creations tend to be the hardest on framerate.

We’ve already rolled out a number of performance improvements — it was one of the underlying reasons for our recent shift to Unreal Engine 5.4 — and more are in the works.

Finally, we still have to tackle the “ghost town” syndrome, when the world gradually fills up with the homes of inactive players. Work on a more robust system to clean up plots of inactive players has started — more details will come soon.

[h2]Building Bridges Between Players[/h2]
At the heart of any MMO lies one simple truth: connection fuels the experience. That’s why Pax Dei was among the first games to integrate the new [url=https://discord.com/developers/social-sdk]Discord Social SDK[/url]—bringing seamless text chat, friends lists, voice chat, and more into the game.

Our goal is to make it easier for players to communicate, coordinate, and share adventures—whether they're crafting in a village or battling side-by-side.

And because connection also means speaking your language, Pax Dei is now available in German and French, with Polish and Spanish coming soon.

[h2]Closing the loop[/h2]
As a player-driven Social Sandbox MMO, the heart of Pax Dei is very much its economy, thriving not through scripted content but by fostering meaningful social interactions, trade, and competition.

If we take a bird’s eye view, Pax Dei relies on one core engagement loop: Harvest, Create, Destroy — a cycle that empowers players to shape the world of Pax Dei.

Harvest covers actions like cutting wood, mining, hunting, and ‘farming’ PVE enemies for gold and loot. Create encompasses crafting and building systems. While much work remains, these two parts of the loop are now firmly in place.

For the game economy to become self-sustaining on a larger scale—to truly close the loop—we now need to offer players meaningful ways to spend what they earn.

In other words, there must be systems that allow value to be removed from the economy, balancing what’s gained through harvesting and crafting.

By “value,” we mean your gear, gold, and Grace. Don’t worry—your plots remain safe and will continue to be protected under the Pax Dei.

From that perspective, [i][b]Market Square[/b][/i] added two crucial components to the game.

[list]
[*] Market Stalls and the Gold economy allow player-to-player trading, which opens ways for players to specialize. If you prefer playing a crafter rather than a fighter, you now have a way to get the components you need from other players — by selling them the equipment they require for the part of the game they prefer to engage with.
[*] By spending Grace, players can now access effects that will help them progress in the game. We’ve only added a few spells for now, and more are coming. This is one part of the game where we want to give players ample opportunities to feel good about spending some of the value they have accumulated.
[/list]
Balancing the in-game economy will require more work, not only to make it more profound and more rewarding, but also to ensure it's sustainable long term. It’s the reason we will be focusing more on this part of the game loop in the coming months.

[h2]What’s Next[/h2]
Our next major update, Verse 3 - name still to be decided, will mark a significant step forward for Pax Dei. With it, you’ll experience a world that feels more rewarding and more strategic.

We’re making some changes to the combat system by adding several new spells and new characteristics to gear. We are adding a new weapon type, staves, which will be dedicated to healing spells.

Additionally, all melee weapons will have three distinct abilities to further differentiate their playstyles. These additions aim to create a more dynamic combat experience, deepen the interplay between roles, and offer more tactical options.

Whether you prefer the brute force of melee, the steadfastness of a tank, or the supportive role of a healer, you'll find more ways to customize your build.

Naturally, these combat updates will impact the crafting system, particularly Tailoring, Leatherworking, and Blacksmithing. We’re refining onboarding, dependencies, and progression pacing.

We aim to simplify the early game with more intuitive crafting chains, meaningful low-tier items, easier access to spells, and reduced cross-profession dependencies in the first levels.

We’re also adjusting the balance to emphasize gathering over extended crafting sessions.

Another major component of Verse 3 is a world revamp. We aim to increase player density and interaction by adding more Heartlands per Province and slightly reducing the overall size of the Wildlands. While resource locations will shift, biome gathering rules will remain consistent.

Additionally, a new Fast Travel Miracle will be introduced, reshaping how players traverse the world and improving the global economy.

The revamped world will also feature improved starting areas: Petra Dei will offer limited storage for all players and include pre-placed, entry-level public crafting stations, making the onboarding experience smoother and more accessible to newcomers.

[h2]Looking Further Ahead[/h2]
Later this year, we’ll be expanding PvP in meaningful ways. PvP will play a key role in keeping Pax Dei’s economy vibrant and dynamic. Central to this evolution is a reimagined Lyonesse—a larger, high-stakes PvP zone where risk and reward go hand in hand.

Players will battle for control of valuable, exclusive resources, but success won’t come easily.

Coordination, strategy, and bold action will be essential to claim key locations, like what we currently call the Trade Towns.

We’re also planning to introduce new customization options, including a cloth dye system that gives crafters greater creative freedom.

Alongside this, expect quality-of-life improvements—and, if all goes well, mounts may finally make their way into the game.

[h2]Transitioning Beyond Early Access[/h2]
Pax Dei is a live, evolving world — we will continue to deliver meaningful updates as we expand the game.

To sustain this, we’ll soon share more details on our monetization plans designed to support server costs while ensuring fair value for players.

We sincerely appreciate your ongoing support, and we remain committed to delivering an experience that empowers you to shape your own adventures in Pax Dei.

Thank you for being part of this incredible journey — we can’t wait to see what stories you create next.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Spotlight - Upcoming Building Changes
notes.notes:
Hello Paxians,

Last week’s announcement about upcoming building changes led to a lot of questions from the community. Many of you wanted more information on the reasons behind these changes and what they might mean for building and crafting in the future.

Let’s do a deep dive into the upcoming changes with answers to all (or almost all) your questions.

[h2]Why make changes?[/h2]

Building in Pax Dei is about creativity and expression, but some inconsistencies in material costs have made certain choices feel less intuitive. We want players to design their structures based on aesthetics rather than minor differences in resource costs. Additionally, we’ve found that some crafting recipes were more complicated than necessary, slowing down the building process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/a4cacf9d2ed42071a28cb906e59687e4b452c720.png[/img]
Our goal with these changes is twofold:
[olist]
[*] Consistency –  Comparable building pieces should have uniform costs, ensuring that your taste and aesthetics drive your choices more than the cost constraints. We also unified the unlock levels of the sets.
[list]
[*] Note that some pieces have moved level, such as half-timber railings, which have been moved from level 16 to 30. They have been unified into the building sets more accurately.
[*] New floor pieces have been added to all sets, and the old half-timber floors have been moved to level 30.
[/list]
[*]Simplification – Reducing the variety of materials required for each piece will enhance crafting accessibility while maintaining depth and variety.
[/olist]
We understand that some of you may worry these changes will make the game feel "too simple," but we want to reassure you that this is not our intention, nor is it the future of Pax Dei. As stated above, our goal is to make Pax Dei more accessible to newcomers while maintaining long-term challenges.
For the next content update, we are adjusting the building system and will continue refining other systems as needed. We are always reviewing balance and player feedback to ensure that crafting, building, and the overall game experience remain engaging and rewarding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/cbbb46aba8b74e0e9875c3187daf43344100bf6f.png[/img]
[h2]What’s changing?[/h2]
In the upcoming content update - Market Square Part 3 - we’re making the following adjustments:
Wall and roof costs:

[list]
[*] Walls and walls with windows will now cost the same, letting players choose based on looks rather than a small price difference.
[*] Roof pieces and roof with windows pieces will also cost the same, following the same logic.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/608ed97f1f92d1586afc04f1246120191b5a7d29.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Triangular pieces adjustments:
[list]
[*] Triangular walls will now cost approximately half of a regular wall, rounded up to the nearest whole number. For example if a regular wall costs 25, a triangular wall will cost 13 (12.5 rounded up).
[*] Triangular foundations will cost exactly half of a full foundation.
[/list]
[*] Crafting recipe streamlining:
[list]
[*] Wooden pegs are being removed as building materials as they were an extra step in construction and didn’t add much value. Once the content update is released, pegs that were used for building pieces will not be refunded on destruction. We know you’re sad not to be able to use them anymore for building, but as they won’t be removed from your inventories, you can still keep the ones you have in your storage for the future recycling feature (no ETA on this one yet though). 
[*] Each building piece will now require only two types of materials (in varying amounts) among the vast selection of materials available for building, simplifying the crafting process without taking away from the experience of crafting and building.
[/list]
[*] Clay node adjustments:
[list]
[*]  The number of Clay nodes is being reduced by half, but each node will now yield twice as much Clay—so the overall resource gain remains the same but with fewer interactions required.
[/list]
[*]New pieces:
[list]
[*]We’re completing existing sets (foundation, hut, cottage, half-timber), particularly with new beams and floors.
[/list]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/b96ad8f07b0c8be12a7feaf8364babf5350d9012.png[/img]
[h2]What does that mean for me as a player?[/h2]

These changes mean a more intuitive and faster building experience. You’ll spend less time managing excessive materials and more time focusing on designing your dream structure.

The simplification of material requirements still means you’ll need to find and process resources, but it removes extra steps that added little to the overall experience, making it easier for both new and experienced players to build efficiently.

For example, a regular wall and a windowed wall now cost the same, so you can choose what you want based on style. Fewer crafting materials per piece also mean less back-and-forth to storage, letting you focus more on building.

[h2]Will other changes be made to crafting or resources?[/h2]

Yes! While the upcoming content update brings these refinements, we’re also working on new building pieces to complement existing sets like cottages, huts, and half-timber structures. 

Additionally, Limestone, Ornamental, and Log set pieces are planned for the next major content update (aka Verse 3), so more customization options are coming.

We look forward to your thoughts and feedback on the upcoming changes to building in this Discord [url=https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1339582027200204840]dedicated thread[/url].

As stated already, this is still a work in progress, so a few changes might occur before the next content patch is deployed to the live shards. Keep an eye out for more spotlights coming in soon. 

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Market Square Part 2 - Patch Notes
notes.notes:
[h2]New features[/h2]

[h3]Grace: Essence of the Divine’s power[/h3]
[list]
[*] Grace is an ethereal currency central to player progression, rewards, and social systems in Pax Dei. It symbolizes the Divine's power, enabling you to perform miracles for yourself or those you care about.
[/list]
[b]How to Acquire Grace[/b]
[list]
[*] Daily Login: Receive a small amount of Grace for free each day just by logging in.
[*] Gold Exchange: Spend gold to acquire additional Grace. However, the cost increases progressively—the more Grace you buy in a single day, the more expensive each point becomes. This scaling resets every 24 hours (real-time).
[/list]
[b]How Grace Works[/b]
[list]
[*] Once obtained, Grace can be spent to perform miracles that provide powerful abilities, bonuses, or practical utilities. There’s no limit to how much Grace you can accrue, and your total Grace pool is shared across all your characters within the same server region (EU, US, or AP).
[*] You can track your current Grace balance in the Grace menu and unlock its potential to shape your journey in Pax Dei.
[*] Grace will be developed and become more prominent with future patches.
[/list]
[h3]Miracles: Unlocking Divine Powers[/h3]

Miracles are powerful and thematic abilities designed to enhance your experience in Pax Dei. Whether you're focused on exploration, crafting, combat, or socializing, there’s a Miracle for every playstyle and level of wealth. They allow you to perform supernatural feats, receive divine blessings, and harness extraordinary powers to shape your journey.

[b]Costs and Accessibility[/b]
[list]
[*] Most Miracles require Grace to cast, though some are free. Notably, familiar abilities like the home Teleport and corpse-summoning miracles (previously in the utility menu, T) are now integrated into the new Miracle menu and remain free of Grace cost.
[*] You can access the Miracle menu by pressing T.
[/list]
[b]Introducing New Miracles[/b]
[list]
[*] The first wave of new Miracles in this patch focuses on boosting your gathering and crafting efficiency.
[*] These essential blessings are automatically granted to all players.
[*] Additional Miracles will be introduced over time, many of which will require exploration and progression to unlock.
[/list]
[h3]New Miracles: Gathering and Profession Blessings[/h3]

[b]Gathering Blessings[/b]

Gathering blessings increase the efficiency of specific resource-gathering activities, offering bonus yields when active. These blessings have a duration of 1 hour and can be refreshed by recasting the same Miracle. Different gathering blessings can be used simultaneously.
[list]
[*] Bountiful Harvest: Increases yield from gathering plants, mushrooms, and other gathering nodes.
[*] Prospector’s Blessing: Boosts yield from mining nodes.
[*] Nature’s Favor: Enhances yield from tree chopping.
[*] Hunter’s Favor: Improves yield from skinning (e.g., hide drops).
[/list]
[b]Profession Blessings[/b]

Profession blessings temporarily enhance crafting skills, increasing the success rate of crafting tasks and, in turn, accelerating XP gains. These blessings do not impact XP rewards directly or unlock recipes, as the base skill is used for those purposes.
[list]
[*] Different profession blessings can be active at the same time.
[*] If two blessings boost the same skill, only the strongest buff applies (e.g., Armorer’s and Weapon Smith’s blessings both buff Blacksmithing but won’t stack).
[/list]
These blessings also have a duration of 1 hour and can be refreshed by recasting the same Miracle.
[list]
[*] Alchemist’s Blessing: +1 Alchemy.
[*] Baker’s Blessing: +1 Baking.
[*] Carpenter’s Blessing: +1 Carpentry.
[*] Cook’s Blessing: +1 Cooking and Charcuterie.
[*] Jeweler’s Blessing: +1 Jewelry Making.
[*] Tailor’s Blessing: +1 Tailoring.
[*] Winemaker’s Blessing: +1 Winemaking and Brewing.
[*] Armorer’s Blessing: +1 Armor Smithing and Blacksmithing.
[*] Weapon Smith’s Blessing: +1 Weapon Smithing and Blacksmithing.
[*] Hunter’s Blessing: +1 Leatherworking and Fletching.
[/list]
[b]Future Plans[/b]

In the future, higher-tier versions of these blessings will be introduced. These upgraded Miracles will offer greater benefits, come at a higher Grace cost, and may require unlocking through exploration and progression. We also plan to introduce other types of Miracles, such as ones that facilitate traveling.
Miracles are just the beginning of what Pax Dei has in store—let the Divine guide you on your path!

notes.title: Market Square - Patch Notes & Known issues
notes.notes:
[h2]Hello Paxians![/h2]
First, here is the content recap for Verse 2, Market Square (with a little teaser about the next update with Grace and Miracles):
[previewyoutube=3yiUpkrGOJM;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]New Feature: Gold and Markets[/h2]
[h3]Gold[/h3]
[list]
[*] You can now obtain Gold in the game:
[list]
[*] Kill some humanoid NPCs and check what they drop;
[*] Gold operates as an 'ethereal currency' represented only in the UI;
[*] When you receive Gold, the system adds it to a wallet in your inventory;
[*] You can transfer Gold from your wallet to any chest where it will also appear as in a wallet;
[*] Your Gold balance is unaffected by your avatar's death and can't be looted in PvP.
[/list][/list]
[h2]Market Stalls[/h2]
[list]
[*] You can build Market Stalls to sell and buy items for Gold.
[list]
[*]Market Stalls are available with Carpentry level 5.
[*]The recipe will appear in the crafters' list.
[*]Each Market Stall has a maximum capacity of active sell orders. Currently, this limit is at 120 per Market Stall.
[/list]
[*] Permissions - currently only the Market Stall’s owner can change them
[list]
[*]You can set the following permissions to determine who can sell goods at your Market Stall:
[list]
[*]Private,
[*]Clan,
[*]Clan - Elders,
[*]Clan - Alderman.
[/list]
[*]Actions you can't change the permission for:
[list]
[*]Everyone can purchase from any Market Stall,
[*]An order can be canceled by the seller, the Market Stall owner, or the plot owner.
[/list][/list]
[*] Creating a sell order
[list]
[*]Put an item or a stack of items from your inventory on sale and give it a gold price. Each sell order size corresponds to one inventory slot.
[*]Creating a sell order comes at a brokering fee gold charge.
[*]This can only be done if the Market Stall is not at full capacity, the player can afford the broker's fee, and the player has sell permission.
[*]Once created, each sell order shows the item, the stack size, the seller name, and the price. 
[*]Items with less than 100% durability and lifetime can still be sold. The buyer can see the durability state of the item in the details panel.
[/list]
[*] Market Stalls don't yet have detailed filters or sorting options, but you can use the text search to filter items by name or by the seller's name.
[list]
[*]You can also use a quick filter for a single item type by hovering over an item or sell order and pressing the input displayed as “Filter by item. “ This option automatically sets the item's name into the text search filter.
[/list]
[*] Purchasing an item
[list]
[*]Anyone can browse any Market Stall and purchase items from it.
[*]You can only purchase an item when you have available inventory space and carry enough Gold to afford it.
[*]Upon purchase, Gold is immediately transferred to the seller's avatar wallet.
[/list]
[*] Canceling an order
[list]
[*]Orders can only be canceled by the seller, the Market Stall owner, and the plot owner.
[*]You can only cancel an order if you have free inventory space to withdraw it.
[*]Canceling an order withdraws the item from the stall and [b]places it in the inventory of the player who canceled it.[/b] As with the permissions on your plot(s), you must trust the people you work with!
[*]When an order is canceled, the fee spent upon creation is lost.
[/list]
[*] Market Stall Notifications
[list]
[*] When your sell order is filled out, you receive the gold immediately in your wallet.
[*] The initial release of the Market Stalls doesn't give you a visual notification when you sell a good. Your gold wallet updates as gold is transferred to it. We're still working on clear notifications for this and a Market Log where you review your active orders and trade activity.
[/list]
[*] Destroying a Market Stall
[list]
[*]Market Stall can only be destroyed if it has no active sell orders. The plot owner, the market stall owner, or the sell order owner(s) must cancel any active orders to be able to destroy a market stall.
[/list]
[*] If a plot with a Marker Stall is released:
[list]
[*] As there is no plot owner anymore, only the Market Stall owner and the owners of the different sell orders can cancel the orders.
[*] If someone now places a plot on top of the Market Stall, they become the plot’s owner and obtain rights on the Market Stall. This means they can empty it by canceling all orders and getting all the goods. Again, be careful with who you work with on the Market Stalls.
[/list][/list]

[h2]Changes & Fixes[/h2]
[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] A lot of stack sizes have been increased. 
[*] The system for selecting interactable items—loots, gatherables, and props—is now more reliable when the items are stacked on each other.
[*] The interaction range has also been slightly increased.
[*] The Unstuck ability can no longer be used during combat and now requires full stamina to activate.
[*] Mining and tree-chopping animations have been enhanced.
[*] Clan names will now consistently appear below player names in character nameplates.
[/list]

[h2]Combat Balance and fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Projectiles can now penetrate water surfaces.
[*] Reduced forward movement of all melee attacks by 10%.
[*] The stamina cost of blocking in PvE combat has been reduced.
[*] Base stamina regeneration is paused during blocking, but food and potion regeneration will continue.
[*] The melee targeting has been improved to prioritize enemies close by.
[*] The melee Aim Assist slider has been removed from the game.
[*] The damage of all sword types has been increased.
[*] Combat skills for one-handed and two-handed spears have been divided into Handspears and Polearms  categories.
[*] Fixed an issue where One Handed Spears incorrectly used Polearm damage on the final combo-chain attack.
[*] The area of effect range of the two-handed mace special attack has been reduced.
[*] Balanced the damage output of maces and spears to better align with their utility.
[*] The axe special attack now reduces target physical resistances by 20% (used to be flat value).
[*] The Hurt Proc effect has been adjusted to reduce stun duration, application chance, and flat damage.
[*] Spell Casting now correctly displays the spell icon and text on NPCs' nameplates.
[*] Fixed an issue where attempting to cast a spell on cooldown would prevent subsequent casts in the same slot.
[*] Enemies stuck attempting to path to their target will now teleport to a valid spot near their target. This is a temporary workaround to a dungeon exploit where the enemy movement is blocked so they cannot reach their target.
[*] NPCs will now verify their teleport destination to prevent unintended teleportation.
[*] Fixed issues related to NPC disappearance, aggro, and pathfinding.
[*] Fixed over-prediction of attacks against enemies moving near the player where some hits would be considered being done from behind, ignoring the blocking mitigation.
[*] Fixed an exploit where it was possible to drop an item during combat and “hide” behind it to prevent receiving damages.
[/list]

[h2]Audio[/h2]
[list]
[*] Improved Inquisitor grunts and sounds when fighting in groups.
[*] Fixed the frequency of noises enemies make while idling.
[/list]

[h2]Discord[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added several clan and party events to broadcast to the chat, e.g., new members joining, members leaving, or being kicked out…
[*] Added a settings menu to the general chat that allows players to filter what chat lobbies they see.
[*] Removed the Discord account name displayed in the chat under the player character’s name. The Discord account name information is still available in the interaction menu when clicking on a player's chat entry.
[*] Updated the Discord button textures and text so they should not appear pixelated or blurry at different UI scales.
[*] Fixed several issues with the Direct Message button usability. 
[*] Fixed an issue in which the friend requests, clan invites, and party invites were also displayed to the requester.
[*] Fixed an issue where the nearby chat lobby might not appear in the general chat lobby selector.
[*] Fixed an issue where you couldn't DM a player from the chat interaction menu after sending them a friend request.
[*] Fixed an issue where texts with a line break pasted into the chat would automatically be sent.
[*] Fixed an issue where successfully linking your account to Discord from the chat settings or friend list wouldn't trigger a pop-up.
[/list]

[h2]World[/h2]
[list]
[*] Increased the size of the Skullcap resource for better visibility.
[*] Added a missing icon for Green Apples.

notes.title: Massive Pax Dei update overhauls nearly every part of the MMORPG
notes.notes:
The idea of a world where everything is made by players is a compelling one, and it's something Pax Dei is attempting to make manifest. Similar to other social survival titles like Conan Exiles, Rust, or Valheim, Pax Dei contains a huge open world filled with monsters to slay, humans to fear, resources to gather, and plots you can build upon. Released back in June, its first content update has now arrived, and almost every aspect of the game has been altered, but be warned - there's a downside too.
